trends.name: Iran Ceasefire Fragility & Hormuz Blockade
trends.summary: Iran's President threatens to back out of ceasefire after Israeli violations; Iran restricting Strait of Hormuz to 15 vessels/day maximum, creating critical oil supply bottleneck. This geopolitical risk is reshaping energy markets and forcing traders to reassess 'war's over' rally positioning. Oil remains elevated but fragile below $100/bbl.

trends.name: PCE Inflation Sticky at 3.0% Core
trends.summary: February Core PCE came in at 3.0% YoY and 0.4% MoM, matching expectations exactly but remaining well above Fed's 2% target. This is the final pre-Iran war inflation datapoint, signaling sticky price pressures persist despite recent disinflation narrative. Fed policy path now uncertain given geopolitical disruption.

trends.name: Mega-Cap AI Capex Arms Race Intensifies
trends.summary: Amazon CEO Jassy explicitly stated 'We are not going to be conservative' on $200B AI spending; Meta commits additional $21B to CoreWeave for AI infrastructure; Google-Intel partnership expands for AI chips. Capex competition is reaching unprecedented scale, forcing investors to reconsider AI profitability timelines and ROIC thresholds.

trends.name: Personal Income Collapse & Wage Weakness
trends.summary: February Personal Income fell 0.1% MoM—only the second negative print since late 2021—while Personal Spending rose just 0.5% (below 0.6% estimate). Real Personal Spending barely moved at 0.1%, indicating household purchasing power erosion and potential consumer slowdown ahead despite soft landing narrative.

trends.name: Labor Market Softening Signals Emerging
trends.summary: Initial Jobless Claims came in at 219K (above 210K estimate), and 40%+ of employed workers hold non-degree jobs (highest since 2020)—signaling labor market bifurcation and potential wage pressure from lower-skill workers. Continuing claims at 1.794M suggest underlying employment stress despite headlines.

trends.name: Dollar Weakness & Purchasing Power Erosion
trends.summary: $100 in 2021 was worth only $80 by 2026—the largest five-year purchasing power loss since 2005. This represents critical currency debasement affecting consumer real returns, international capital flows, and long-duration asset valuations. Implications for inflation hedges and commodity allocations are significant.

trends.name: Earnings Boom Catalyst for Equity Upside
trends.summary: Earnings season expectations point to a major earnings boom that could blindside bearish sentiment, particularly in semiconductors (Nvidia, Micron, ASML) and tech. Strong fundamentals remain intact despite geopolitical noise, with guidance improvements likely to reshape risk-reward for equity markets.

trends.name: Tariff Impact 2025 vs 2026: Different Drivers
trends.summary: 2025 vs 2026 tariff shocks show same negative GDP impact but driven by different policy mechanisms, creating compounding uncertainty for multinationals and supply chains. Constellation Brands already withdrew 2028 guidance due to tariff/Mexico uncertainties, signaling corporates losing visibility.

trends.name: Semiconductor Momentum & Memory Shift
trends.summary: Micron, Intel, and ASML all showing strong momentum; memory bottleneck shifting in ways market hasn't priced in; Intel's hot streak continuing with Google partnership wins. AI-driven semiconductor demand remains structural tailwind, but valuations stretched—creates select-stock opportunity vs broad ETF plays.

trends.name: Bond Volatility & Rate Uncertainty New Normal
trends.summary: Government bond yields whipsawing as interest rate uncertainty becomes endemic; inflation data conflicts with geopolitical shocks creating unpredictable Fed reaction function. Fixed income investors face compounding volatility from both data surprises and regime-shift risk in monetary policy.

trends.name: Oil & Airline Dynamics: Crack Spread Squeeze
trends.summary: Higher crack spreads (refining margins) are pressuring airline profitability as fuel costs rise; American and Southwest both facing margin compression despite volume recovery. Hormuz restrictions amplify this dynamic, threatening airline earnings despite strong leisure travel demand. Fee increases signal pricing power erosion.

trends.name: GLP-1 Demand Driving Retail & Fashion Spending
trends.summary: Millions adopting GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are turning to retailers to refresh wardrobes, creating unexpected consumer spending catalyst in apparel and discretionary retail. This sector-specific demand tailwind is offsetting broader consumer spending weakness and represents emerging thematic opportunity.
